column2: Réminiscences de Norma (Bellini)
You will have heard that the ladies fight over my gloves?
With one piano I will give you more sound than an orchestra.
Mendelssohn
Revival of Bach's St Matthew Passion
In 1829 he revived Bach's St Matthew Passion after about a hundred years. Gewandhaus Kapellmeister from 1835.
Fantasia on Rossini's Moïse Op. 33
He took the age by storm with his 'three-hand' technique, wrapping the melody in arpeggios from both hands. In 1837 he faced Liszt in a contest.
His instrument was the Guarneri del Gesù 'Il Cannone'. Rumours of a pact with the Devil never left him.
Nocturne in E-flat major Op. 9 No. 2
Playing before a crowd takes my breath away.
With you… perhaps I could play outside the salon as well.
Paris debut at the Salle Pleyel on 26 February 1832. He preferred the intimate salon to the large hall.
Grandes études de Paganini: No. 3 'La campanella'
To me the piano is an orchestra in itself.
Very well. I will stand beside you as the Paganini of the piano.
In April 1832 he heard Paganini play and resolved, it is said, to become 'the Paganini of the piano'.
Symphonie fantastique: 5th movement (Dies irae)
Is there an orchestra in this world big enough to play my scores?
At last, someone who understands! Kindly provide an orchestra of four hundred.
In 1838 Paganini gave 20,000 francs to Berlioz, the composer of Harold en Italie.
Overture to Guillaume Tell
I write no more operas. Now, about tonight's menu.
Very well. But luncheon is to be a full course every day.
After Guillaume Tell in 1829 he laid down his opera pen and went down in history as a gourmet.
Truffles, foie gras, and the finest chef — they shall be yours.
Beethoven: Symphony No. 5 in C minor
To play Beethoven as he should be played. Nothing else interests me.
Your orchestra will perform all of Beethoven's symphonies. That is my condition.
In 1828 he founded the Société des Concerts du Conservatoire and brought Beethoven's symphonies to France.
Viotti: Violin Concerto No. 22
Acrobatics are not the art of the violin.
For the honour of the French school, I will be the keystone of your orchestra.
Violin professor at the Paris Conservatoire. In 1834 he published his method, L'Art du violon.
Chopin: Cello Sonata Op. 65
If Frédéric does not go, neither do I.
Gladly. The cello is the heart of an orchestra.
Chopin's close friend. Chopin's last major work, the Cello Sonata Op. 65, is dedicated to him.
From Bellini's La sonnambula
Where is the stage worthy of my voice?
I will sing — if your orchestra can stand up to my voice.
A legendary mezzo-soprano. Her huge range and fiery acting drove London and Paris wild.
24 Études Op. 70
Herr Beethoven's way is the true tradition.
I place my London connections, all of them, in your hands.
He prepared the piano-vocal score of Beethoven's Fidelio. Later he taught at the Leipzig Conservatory.
Solo for double bass
Would you care to see my collection of dolls?
Without the bass an orchestra is just a noise. Leave it to me.
Double-bass virtuoso, also known as a collector of dolls. A friend of Beethoven.
A nobleman does not make exaggerated gestures.
As a gentleman, I will join your orchestra.
A set of waltzes
Vienna turns in three-four time.
Let us spread the waltz evening all over Europe.
The 'father of the waltz', who led his orchestra with violin in hand. He and Lanner divided the public between them.
Beethoven: String Quartet Op. 127
I am busy training my pupils, you know.
I will put the strings in order.
He took part in performing Beethoven's late quartets and trained Joachim and others; founder of the Viennese violin school.
30 Études Op. 849
First, a hundred scales. Then we talk.
If it can be between writing a thousand études.
Pupil of Beethoven and teacher of the boy Liszt. He left an enormous number of études.
Schumann: Piano Concerto in A minor
I will not bend the composer's intention by a single note.
If you will let me play Robert's music as well.
Gewandhaus debut at nine. Later Schumann's wife, she was called the greatest woman pianist of the nineteenth century.
Abegg Variations Op. 1
Florestan and Eusebius are still arguing, you see.
Hats off, gentlemen. I shall write for you.
The theme of his Op. 1 is A–B♭–E–G–G: 'Abegg'. In 1834 he founded the Neue Zeitschrift für Musik.
'Casta diva' from Norma
The long, long melody is everything.
Let us build an orchestra that can sing my melodies.
Norma was first performed at La Scala in 1831. A composer Chopin deeply revered.
Title role in Norma
Only I can sing Norma.
On the stage, I am queen.
The soprano who created the title roles of Norma and La sonnambula.
Mad scene from Lucia di Lammermoor
I shall finish the next opera in two weeks.
No one writes faster than I do.
Astonishingly fast, he left nearly seventy operas. Lucia di Lammermoor was first performed in Naples in 1835.
Demonstration of the new flute
Look at this key mechanism. The intonation is perfectly even.
The tone of the new flute — in your orchestra.
In 1832 he presented a flute with a new key mechanism: the creator of the 'Boehm system', the basis of the modern flute.
Weber: Clarinet Concerto No. 1
Weber wrote his concertos for me, you know.
I will lend you the clarinet's singing heart.
The virtuoso for whom Weber wrote his clarinet concertos and Concertino.
Improvisation (in the Mozart tradition)
Is there anyone on this continent who can beat me at improvising?
In the name of my master Mozart, I will help you.
As a boy he lived and studied in Mozart's house. The finest improviser of his day; Kapellmeister at Weimar from 1819.
Prelude to Tristan und Isolde
Do not ask about my debts. Let us talk about the music of the future.
Build me a theatre of my own and I am yours, soul and all.
The opening 'Tristan chord' (F–B–D♯–G♯) is said to have changed the history of harmony. Court Kapellmeister in Dresden from 1843.
A Life for the Tsar
Russian songs, in the Russian tongue.
The sound of Russia, carried to Europe.
'Father of Russian music'. A Life for the Tsar was first performed in 1836.
A pact with the Devil? Well now, who can say.
An interesting young man. I will lend you my bow.
His instrument was the Guarneri del Gesù 'Il Cannone' (the Cannon).
Beethoven: Symphony No. 9 in D minor Op. 125 'Choral'
The War of Music
Wagner versus Brahms

The opening of the Bayreuth Festspielhaus and the completion of Brahms's First Symphony. The age of the 'War of the Romantics', when the New German school and the champions of absolute music split the musical world. In Milan, Verdi waits.
Absolute music party
New German school
Theatre and virtuoso party
Musikverein, Vienna (the Golden Hall)
The critic Hanslick
The great hall of the Musikverein, completed in 1870. Brahms was the society's artistic director for three years from 1872.
Paris Opéra (Palais Garnier)
The director-general
The Palais Garnier, completed in 1875.
Royal Opera House, Covent Garden
Gewandhaus subscribers
Bavarian court opera
The theatre where Tristan und Isolde (1865) and Die Meistersinger (1868) were first performed.
Dresden court opera (Semperoper)
Provisional Theatre, Prague
The theatre committee
A theatre for performances in Czech. Smetana was its principal conductor.
Royal Hungarian Academy of Music
President Liszt
The Budapest audience
Founded in 1875. Liszt was its first president.
Mariinsky Theatre

Revolutionary of the music drama. Supreme in expression and theory, weak in technique, and always short of money. As in real life his time runs out in February 1883, so you must win before then. Keep the festival theatre going with Ludwig II's subsidy (+400 a month).
Ludwig II's subsidy (+400 a month)
'Ride of the Valkyries' from Die Walküre
Siegfried Idyll
His Majesty the King of Bavaria has built a theatre for me, you know.
The music of the future is already sounding in my head.
A stern figure seen as Beethoven's heir. His weapons are theory and sound finances. Publishing contract with Simrock (+250 a month).
Publishing contract with Simrock (+250 a month)
Symphony No. 1: finale (the alphorn theme)
Variations and Fugue on a Theme by Handel Op. 24
Piano Concerto No. 1 in D minor
Herr Hanslick has been praising my work to the skies, you see.
I have come this far with Beethoven's footsteps at my back.
The 'Tristan chord' (F–B–D♯–G♯) is said to have changed the history of harmony.
Symphony No. 1 in C minor
The First Symphony took some twenty years to complete. So heavy was Beethoven's shadow.
'La donna è mobile' from Rigoletto
Born in 1813, the same year as Wagner. He stands at the summit of Italian opera.
Les jeux d'eaux à la Villa d'Este (1877)
Between prayers, if that will do.
If these old hands will serve, they are yours.
First president of the Royal Hungarian Academy of Music, founded in 1875. His daughter Cosima became Wagner's wife.
Symphony No. 4 'Romantic'
Master Wagner is, to me, the god of music.
For God and the Master, I will write symphonies.
He dedicated his Third Symphony to Wagner. A master of organ improvisation, acclaimed in Paris in 1869 and London in 1871.
Der Ring des Nibelungen, complete
I have my hands full preparing Bayreuth.
One baton — I entrust it to you.
In 1876 he conducted the first complete Ring at the first Bayreuth Festival. With the Vienna Philharmonic he also gave the premiere of Brahms's Second Symphony.
The Blue Danube
Wagner and Brahms both like my waltzes, you know.
Never mind the factions — let us dance.
On Frau Strauss's fan Brahms wrote the opening of The Blue Danube and added: 'Unfortunately not by Brahms.'
Bach: Chaconne from Partita No. 2 for solo violin
Free but lonely (F–A–E). That is my creed.
I will take up my bow in your orchestra.
He gave the first performance of Brahms's Violin Concerto in 1879. His motto 'F–A–E' gave rise to a sonata written jointly by Schumann and friends.
Wagner's music is beyond my understanding.
If it is to protect Robert's works.
Brahms's lifelong friend. She did not care for Wagner's music.
Helmwige in Die Walküre
Hojotoho! Only joking.
I will lend you a Valkyrie's voice.
At the first Bayreuth Ring in 1876 she sang the Rhinemaiden Woglinde and the Valkyrie Helmwige.
Conductor of the Tristan und Isolde premiere (1865)
…I would ask you not to mention that name.
For the three great Bs: Bach, Beethoven and Brahms.
Conductor of the Tristan premiere. He lost his wife Cosima to Wagner and later became a champion of Brahms.
Symphony No. 9 'From the New World': 2nd movement
I would rather be watching the trains.
The songs of Bohemia, for your orchestra.
In 1877, on Brahms's recommendation, the publisher Simrock issued his works and he became known. A great lover of railways.
Ballet Swan Lake (1877)
I reported on Bayreuth, but frankly, it was too long.
I will write melodies for your orchestra.
In 1876 he covered the first Bayreuth Festival as a newspaper correspondent.
I promise you a pension to rival Madame von Meck's.
At the Fountain Op. 20
Do you know the Russian school of cello playing?
I will hold up the orchestra with the sound of the cello.
The virtuoso Tchaikovsky called 'the tsar of cellists'.
